items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: Claude, I noticed this playing Dickie Wells and all them fellas.

ctx.x: Do you go down into, well you know Roy always said he could play his horn backwards. Yeah. In the six and seven position, do you use that? Or do you go down first and second?

Well I tell you, Claude Jones I think was one of the great trombones, used to be the Fletcher Anderson. Claude, I noticed this playing Dickie Wells and all them fellas. See I always go, whenever this fella was in town, I'd go there, as I said before. And I tried to, I copied, I'm a copycat, see what I'm talking about? And I'd go back home and work on it. Now some leaders don't like much vibrato. You suppose if you're in a section, I mean you suppose a match of tones, you understand what I'm talking about? So Roy,…
When you first started playing, were you playing with Bantam, you were all playing your arrangements? The first band that you played with, was Bernie and John?

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: Yeah, and I just felt like Dickie Wells, he was a wonderful trombone player.

ctx.x: Maybe it was the way Roy Carriott still. I just had to be a football player. Maybe he had the reputation of going to sleep on a job or something, you know?
Yeah, and I just felt like Dickie Wells, he was a wonderful trombone player. He still plays.

I was going to ask again, before I forget it, about Joe Oliver again. Was he really a good pool player? Did he play all the time? Who was that? Joe Oliver. Oh yeah, he was good. You know he had one bad eye.
